title: Thermal relaxation asymmetry persists under inertial effects
summary: Relaxation phenomena far from thermal equilibrium feature a rich phenomenology, including the thermal relaxation asymmetry. The latter states that heating occurs faster than cooling in overdamped harmonic systems quantified in terms of excess free energy and entropy production. Upon isolating the relevant relaxational contribution to the entropy production, we here algebraically prove the asymmetry in thermal relaxation in phase space in the entire range from overdamped dynamics to underdamped dynamics.
